title: Quasi-coherent algebra sheaves and affine-local algebra properties
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For a sheaf $\mathcal A$ of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf], quasi-coherence means that its underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. These algebra sheaves form a full subcategory. Such an algebra is finite, integral, or of finite presentation if on every affine open $U$ its structure map on sections is respectively a finite, integral, or finitely presented ring homomorphism. For a quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal A$, its finite quasi-coherent subalgebras are the subobjects of $\mathcal A$ in algebra sheaves whose source is quasi-coherent and finite, ordered by factorization of their inclusions. Their diagram sends each subobject to its source and each inclusion to the induced algebra morphism.
